title.narrative: Output 1.3: Increased ability for advocacy and evidence-based action by UN, OHCHR and partners.
Extent to which the ability for evidence-based advocacy and action has increased among UN, OHCHR, and partners.

target.value: Advocacy is primarily done by OHCHR, based on information received from the partners regarding cases and issues, it is not systematic
Thematic evidence is gathered and improves evidence from case based data.
There is annual systematic evidence that informs partners' advocacy

title.narrative: Output 1.4: Authorities increased their awareness of human rights conditions within their jurisdictions.
Extent to which authorities' awareness of human rights conditions within their jurisdictions has increased.

target.value: Low and uneven awareness
Senior officials in two line ministries, Law Justice and Parliamentary Affairs, Ministry of Home Affairs are engaged in human rights conversations
The knowledge cascades through the ranks in these two ministries and expanded to at least two more ministries

title.narrative: Output 1.2: A digital data ingestion pipeline to streamline data integration, access, and management for advocacy.
Extent to which the digital data ingestion pipeline enhances data integration, access, and management for advocacy.

target.value: Non existent
A digital pipeline is initiated
The pipeline starts to deliver information periodically

title.narrative: Output 1.1: A structured, systematic data collection process for and with OHCHR, UN and partners
Extent to which the structured, systematic data collection process integrates international human rights norms, standards, and principles.

target.value: OHCHR documents human rights violations within its capacity for advocacy- not systematic, neither comprehensive
A six-monthly comprehensive briefing is prepared with inputs from partners
A data collection, analysis and briefing system with UN and NGO partners is functioning.

title.narrative: OHCHR AND CIVIL SOCIETY HUMAN RIGHTS-BASED ANALYSES AND DATA GUIDE UN COUNTRY TEAMS AND GOVERNMENTAL EFFORTS TO IDENTIFY RISKS AND TRENDS AND PREVENT, MITIGATE, OR RESPOND TO EMERGING CRISES, INCLUDING HUMANITARIAN ACTION.

Extent to which oversight, accountability or protection mechanisms that conform to international human rights standards are in place and/or functioning The analysis is reflected in government's policies, legislative framework, priorities of NHRI, national and international protection systems

target.value: Part of the UNSDCF and the commitment documents but no data is available to suggest it is implementation status
Regular timely and evidence based reports are available to assess the integration of a human rights based approach

title.narrative: Output 2.1: Civil society actors, minorities and grassroots communities increased their awareness of human rights conditions in Bangladesh.
Extent to which civil society actors, minorities, and grassroots communities have increased their awareness of human rights conditions in Bangladesh.

target.value: Since September 2024, only two complaints received by SP mandate holders have resulted in communication.

There are at least ten identified groups with whom UN Human Rights systematically works to build their awareness of the human rights situation in Bangladesh and the relevance of using the international human rights framework.
Members of these groups are well aware of the value and methods of engaging with the UN human rights system and other global and regional mechanisms.

title.narrative: Output 2.3: Enhanced capacity of national protection and prevention mechanisms to prevent human rights violations and abuses.
The extent to which the authorities can implement laws, policies, and practices that prevent human rights violations and abuses in civic space has been enhanced.

target.value: The system was completely eroded and currently some laws and policies negatively impact civic space, the interim government has started to address them
At least three laws/ policies are positively amended/ revised as the implementation mechanism is strengthened with the involvement of civilsociety.
Civic space gets strengthened and can advocate, overall policy framework is sensitive to protecting civic space. The government-civil society partnership is established.

title.narrative: OUTCOME 2: CIVIL SOCIETY, YOUTH, AND GRASSROOTS ORGANISATIONS ARE EMPOWERED TO ENGAGE IN SOCIETAL PROCESSES AND UN INITIATIVES.
Level of meaningful participation of right-holders, especially women and discriminated groups, in selected public processes.

target.value: These groups faced the worst impact of the repression and remain weak
Voices of these groups are included in different civil society forums and different government-civil society interface forums

title.narrative: Output 2.2: Increasing the ability of civil society actors, minorities and grassroots communities, including youth, to advocate for addressing emerging human rights issues at local, national, and international levels.

Extent to which civil society actors, minorities, and grassroots communities, including youth, have increased their ability to advocate for a human rights-based approach to social policy and governance structures at local, national, and international levels.

target.value: This process has been limited, and only after the July uprising did these groups start to be vocal
Organisations and groups that belong to the above-mentioned categories are well equipped with skills and start national and international advocacy.
Some platforms work together, covering an intersection of rights in terms of advocacy.
